eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **Revised Carcinogens, Mutagens and Reprotoxic Substances Directive (CMRD):** This directive sets new Occupational Exposure Limit Values (OELs) for cobalt and its inorganic compounds, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, 1,4-dioxane, and isoprene, and adds welding fumes to the list of hazardous substances in Annex I. Previously, specific EU-wide OELs were not established for these substances, and welding fumes were not explicitly included, meaning worker exposure was less stringently regulated. Now, companies must comply with these new limits and revised safety protocols, with Member States required to transpose the rules into national law within two years of its entry into force, which occurs upon publication in the Official Journal. This significantly strengthens worker protection against work-related cancers and other illnesses across all EU industries.

• **Amendment to the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) Market Stability Reserve (MSR):** A provisional political agreement has been reached to amend the MSR, allowing it to retain up to 700 million emission allowances as a buffer. Previously, the MSR automatically invalidated all emission allowances exceeding 400 million, leading to less flexibility in market response. This amendment aims to reinforce the MSR's long-term operational capacity, enhancing the stability and predictability of the EU carbon market. This provides greater certainty for businesses and investors, encouraging investment in industrial decarbonisation efforts.

• **Council Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2324 lifting rule of law measures for Hungary:** This decision formally lifts measures that protected the Union budget against breaches of the principles of the rule of law in Hungary, and repeals the previous Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/2506. Previously, Hungary faced restrictions on accessing certain EU funds due to rule of law concerns, impacting its national budget and potentially foreign investment. With the lifting of these measures, Hungary can now access previously withheld EU funds, which could significantly alter the financial and investment landscape within the country.

• **Council Decision (EU) 2026/2351 on Iceland's participation in EU Space Programmes:** This decision concludes an agreement between the European Union and Iceland, establishing the rules for Iceland's participation in the GOVSATCOM component of the Union Space Programme and the Union Secure Connectivity Programme, and for accessing their services. Previously, Iceland did not have a formal framework for participating in and accessing these specific EU space and secure connectivity initiatives. This agreement fosters closer cooperation in space and secure communication technologies, potentially opening new avenues for tech and security-related businesses in both the EU and Iceland.

Why it matters: This week's EU policy developments highlight a critical shift towards reinforcing market stability in the carbon trading system, resolving significant financial blockades for a Member State, and advancing worker protection across industries.

general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **Ukraine Peace Talks:** Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed in principle to resume trilateral peace talks involving Russia, Ukraine, and the United States after November 10. This announcement followed a meeting in St. Petersburg on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, between Putin and U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, which was also joined virtually by Jared Kushner. The agreement signals a potential diplomatic breakthrough in the ongoing conflict, though previous negotiation attempts have faltered. The resumption of high-level peace talks could significantly de-escalate geopolitical tensions in Eastern Europe and potentially stabilize global energy and food markets. [BBC, PBS News]

• **U.S. Heating Oil Reserve & Iran War Impact:** The U.S. government announced plans on October 21, 2026, to loan one-third of its heating oil reserve to markets in an effort to tame rising domestic prices. President Donald Trump attributed these high prices to his ongoing "war on Iran," stating during a campaign rally that he "might have gone too far" in the conflict. This move aims to alleviate immediate consumer costs in the U.S. and signals a potential shift in rhetoric regarding the conflict's economic repercussions. The explicit link by the U.S. President between military action and domestic economic hardship, coupled with drawing from strategic reserves, underscores global energy market fragility and the economic toll of international conflicts. [Reuters]

• **U.S. Climate Policy & Global Warming:** A new United Nations Environment Programme report, released on October 21, 2026, revealed that global warming projections have worsened, with humanity now heading for a 1.2 degrees Celsius rise above current temperatures. The report cited the formal withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and its increased emissions of 133 megatons of CO2 equivalent last year as major contributing factors. This increased warming projection highlights the growing urgency of climate action and puts renewed pressure on international climate negotiations ahead of upcoming summits. The U.S. policy decision has a substantial impact on global efforts to combat climate change, directly influencing international environmental targets and the severity of future climate-related disasters worldwide. [AP]

• **U.S. Orders Departure from Saudi Arabia:** The U.S. Department of State issued an order on October 21, 2026, for the departure of non-emergency government employees and their family members from its mission in Saudi Arabia. This decision was made due to increased hostilities from Iran-aligned Houthi movement attacks targeting civilian airports and critical infrastructure within the kingdom. The order signals a heightened security risk in Saudi Arabia and could lead to further instability in the Gulf region, impacting travel and economic activities. Escalating tensions and direct threats to international personnel in a key oil-producing region could disrupt global energy supplies and draw in other international actors, as France has already pledged military support to Saudi Arabia. [Al Jazeera]

• **Ebola Case in Nigeria:** Nigerian health officials confirmed the country's first case of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola on October 21, 2026, involving a woman who traveled from Uganda to the capital, Abuja, on October 3. This marks the initial spread of this particular Ebola strain to West Africa in the current outbreak, which has primarily affected the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) is initiating contact tracing and public health measures to contain the spread of the virus. The emergence of a new Ebola strain in a highly populated West African nation poses a significant global health security risk, potentially leading to a broader regional or international public health crisis. [Al Jazeera]

Why it matters: Today's stories collectively underscore a period of escalating global instability across geopolitical, economic, and public health domains, demanding urgent international cooperation to mitigate widespread risks.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
• **Redução da Retenção na Fonte de IRS:** O Despacho n.º 12523-A/2026, publicado a 14 de outubro de 2026, determina uma redução de 50% nas retenções na fonte de Imposto sobre o Rendimento das Pessoas Singulares (IRS) aplicáveis aos rendimentos do trabalho dependente e às pensões pagos em novembro de 2026, incluindo o subsídio de Natal. Anteriormente, as retenções na fonte de IRS eram calculadas com base nas tabelas em vigor sem esta redução adicional. Agora, para o mês de novembro, os cidadãos verão metade da retenção habitual aplicada. Esta medida permite aos cidadãos portugueses antecipar os benefícios de uma descida do IRS aprovada para 2026, resultando num aumento imediato do rendimento disponível em novembro.

• **Regulação do Acesso de Estrangeiros Não Residentes ao Serviço Nacional de Saúde (SNS):** A Assembleia da República aprovou, a 16 de outubro de 2026, projetos de lei que visam regulamentar o acesso de cidadãos estrangeiros não residentes ao SNS. As novas disposições exigirão comprovativos de morada ou de seguro de saúde para o acesso a cuidados não urgentes e reforçarão os mecanismos de cobrança dos serviços prestados. Previamente, o acesso era menos regulado, resultando em desafios na identificação e recuperação de custos. Com esta aprovação, o acesso ao SNS por não residentes tornar-se-á mais restritivo e sujeito a pagamento ou cobertura por seguro, com o objetivo de otimizar a sustentabilidade financeira do sistema.

• **Prorrogação da Alteração Temporária dos Limites Mínimos de Impostos sobre Produtos Petrolíferos e Energéticos:** A Lei n.º 64/2026, de 19 de outubro de 2026, prorroga a vigência da Lei n.º 12-B/2026, que temporária e excecionalmente alterou os limites mínimos das taxas unitárias do imposto sobre os produtos petrolíferos e energéticos. Anteriormente, a Lei n.º 12-B/2026 tinha um prazo de vigência definido, após o qual as taxas poderiam reverter aos limites anteriores ou aumentar. Agora, com a prorrogação, os limites mínimos alterados (e provavelmente mais favoráveis) destas taxas serão mantidos, evitando um potencial aumento nos impostos sobre combustíveis e energia. Esta medida continuará a influenciar os custos de combustível e energia para consumidores e empresas em Portugal.

• **Atualização dos Coeficientes de Desvalorização da Moeda para 2026:** A Portaria n.º 457/2026/1, de 15 de outubro de 2026, atualiza os coeficientes de desvalorização da moeda a aplicar aos bens e direitos alienados durante o ano de 2026. Anteriormente, não havia coeficientes de desvalorização da moeda especificamente atualizados para 2026. Agora, estes novos coeficientes permitem ajustar o valor de aquisição de bens para efeitos de cálculo de mais-valias, aumentando o custo fiscalmente relevante de um ativo e, consequentemente, reduzindo a mais-valia tributável. Esta atualização beneficia os cidadãos e empresas que vendam bens ou direitos em 2026, pois pode levar a uma redução do imposto a pagar sobre as mais-valias.

Why it matters: A redução de 50% na retenção na fonte de IRS em novembro representa um alívio financeiro imediato e tangível para a maioria dos cidadãos portugueses, impactando diretamente o seu poder de compra antes do final do ano.

investment_markets.title: Markets & Economy
investment_markets.content:
SECTOR ALERTS

• **Gold & Silver:** Precious metals saw significant declines today, with gold dropping over 1% to its lowest level since October 14, and silver falling over 2.5%, largely due to a resurgence in U.S. Treasury yields and a strengthening dollar. Elevated energy prices and persistent inflation fears are leading markets to anticipate a prolonged period of restrictive monetary policy from the Federal Reserve, increasing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets. This macroeconomic environment, coupled with inflation fears fueled by geopolitical tensions impacting oil, directly pressures Pedro's precious metals holdings.

• **Oil & Gas — WTI Oil:** WTI crude oil surged by nearly 2% today, with Brent crude surpassing $110 per barrel, driven by escalating geopolitical tensions, including drone strikes on a Saudi Aramco oilfield and Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil infrastructure. These incidents have heightened concerns about energy supply disruptions. Separately, OPEC+ nations reaffirmed their commitment on October 4, 2026, to maintain November 2026 crude oil production targets at September 2026 levels, further contributing to market tightness amid supply concerns. The rising oil prices due to supply fears and unchanged OPEC+ production targets present a favorable outlook for Pedro's energy and oil & gas investments.

• **Equities & Indices — Alphabet (GOOGL):** Alphabet's stock declined 1.62% today, despite reporting strong Q3 2026 earnings on July 22nd, which included a 24.2% revenue growth and an 82% increase in Google Cloud. The market's reaction appears to reflect ongoing concerns about the company's heavy capital expenditures related to AI infrastructure. This suggests investor scrutiny of AI spending even amidst strong underlying business performance.

• **Equities & Indices — Nvidia (NVDA):** Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, speaking in Berlin yesterday, advocated for modular data centers to accelerate the development of Europe's lagging AI sector. This initiative underscores Nvidia's continued strategic focus on building out critical AI infrastructure. Nvidia is also part of an industry taskforce cautioning UK ministers about potential public opposition that could impede future data center construction. This demonstrates Nvidia's proactive role in shaping the global AI ecosystem, which is positive for Pedro's tech holdings.

• **Equities & Indices — Tesla (TSLA):** Tesla's stock gained over 3% today following CEO Elon Musk's strong public endorsement of a potential merger between Tesla and SpaceX, a deal with a combined market value of approximately $3.7 trillion that could be announced in the first half of 2027. Despite a strong stock performance today, Tesla concurrently cut its 2026 capital expenditure forecast by $5 billion, from over $25 billion to $20 billion, after achieving positive free cash flow in Q3 2026 while spending less than expected on AI and robotics projects. While the merger prospect is a significant catalyst, the reduced capex for AI and robotics raises questions about the pace of investment in these key growth areas for Pedro's tech portfolio.

• **Quantum Computing — QTUM ETF:** Quantum hardware company Alice & Bob announced on October 20, 2026, that it achieved the first non-Clifford gate on cat-qubit hardware as part of France's €500 million PROQCIMA competition. This represents a crucial technical milestone towards achieving universal fault-tolerant quantum computation. This breakthrough represents tangible progress in the foundational technology of quantum computing, a positive long-term indicator for Pedro's QTUM ETF.

• **Clean Energy & Nuclear:** Several initiatives are boosting the clean energy sector: Wisconsin announced $11.5 million in Energy Innovation Grants for clean energy projects, China proposed new rules for electricity spot markets allowing renewable energy and battery storage to participate jointly from January 1, 2027, and Southeast Asia is seeing rapidly rising corporate demand for clean power, including from data centers. Additionally, a "balcony solar bill" has been introduced in the U.S. Congress for the first time, and Australia's solar and battery storage connection pipeline has increased by 43% to 80.9 GW. These developments reflect strong global tailwinds for clean energy, driven by policy, regulatory support, and increasing demand from various sectors.

• **Crypto:** The OCC's new waiver rule requires existing US stablecoin issuers awaiting approval to obtain a waiver to continue operations from January 18, 2027. Separately, the SEC's "Innovation Exemption" is now effective, providing a pathway for US crypto companies to operate nationwide, while comments on the proposed "Regulation Crypto Assets" were due October 20, 2026. The Quantum Alliance, formed on October 15, 2026, also warned that 30.2% of Bitcoin could be at risk from a future quantum attack, although no current quantum computers pose an immediate threat. The evolving regulatory landscape in the US provides some clarity for crypto operations, while the long-term, theoretical threat of quantum computing to Bitcoin's security remains a consideration for Pedro's crypto holdings.

Why it matters: Geopolitical tensions are simultaneously driving up oil prices due to supply fears while pushing down safe-haven gold and silver as rising yields and inflation concerns dominate.

ai_productivity.title: ⚡ AI & Productivity
ai_productivity.content:
• **Mistral:** Voxtral 3, a new multimodal speech-to-speech model, was released on October 21, 2026, enabling AI agents to listen, reason, speak, and act. This model represents an advancement in natural, full-duplex conversational AI, moving beyond traditional text-based interactions to more embodied agentic workflows. A developer can now build complex AI assistants that interact more naturally in real-time, such as a virtual customer service agent that can understand nuanced speech and respond conversationally, directly integrating into voice-activated systems.

• **Notion AI:** Notion released significant AI upgrades between October 19-20, 2026, including a rebuilt AI harness that supports up to 24 hours of task execution, a smarter Auto model router delivering results similar to Opus 5.5 and Astra at 90% lower average cost, and a new unified credit system with personal AI connections. These updates enhance the platform's ability to run complex, long-duration AI tasks more efficiently and cost-effectively, while allowing users to connect their existing OpenAI (and soon Anthropic) accounts. Knowledge workers can now automate multi-step projects, like generating a comprehensive market research report over a full day, within Notion, significantly reducing manual oversight and external tool juggling.

• **Perplexity Computer:** Perplexity launched a new feature on October 20, 2026, allowing its Computer agent to run fully locally on Mac devices, enabling users to interact with private files and native applications without data leaving their device. This significantly enhances data privacy and security for sensitive workflows, offering a local execution environment that was previously unavailable. Developers and researchers handling confidential information can now leverage Perplexity's powerful agentic capabilities to analyze proprietary datasets or generate code snippets directly on their machine, without concern for cloud data transmission.

• **Adobe Acrobat:** Adobe introduced "Stylize" in Acrobat on October 20, 2026, an AI-powered feature that allows users to instantly redesign the layout, formatting, and visual style of existing PDFs using Adobe Express design templates. This new capability transforms plain documents into polished, professional-looking files while preserving the original text and images, offering a significant upgrade over manual design adjustments. A business professional can now effortlessly convert a basic text-heavy report into a visually engaging presentation-ready document by selecting a template, saving hours of design work.

Why it matters: The AI landscape continues to evolve with a clear focus on highly capable, integrated agents that enhance productivity, privacy, and cost-efficiency directly within daily workflows.

us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
• **U.S. Treasury Sanctions on Iran's Shadow Fleet Networks:** The U.S. Department of the Treasury, as part of "Operation Economic Outcast," designated the Panama- and Greece-based law firm Karnakis and Karnakis, five associated individuals, a ship management company (Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading), and shipping agents in Singapore (Amigoz Singapore) and Dubai (Whales Shipping Line) for sanctions. These entities are accused of establishing shell companies and providing other services to conceal and transport Iranian oil, petrochemicals, and steel, thereby generating revenue for Iran's military and weapons programs under Executive Order 13902. This action aims to disrupt illicit Iranian financial networks, potentially impacting global shipping and commodity markets by increasing the cost and risk of engaging with sanctioned entities.

• **Department of Justice Launches Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program (WHIP):** The Department of Justice (DOJ) announced the Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program (WHIP), a three-year pilot initiative designed to incentivize reporting of fraud. The program provides fixed payments ranging from $10,000 to $30,000 for qualifying tips that lead to criminal charges in specified fraud categories. This program is supported by a $25 million commitment from the Department of the Treasury. Previously, most government whistleblower reward programs paid awards only after final resolution, including forfeiture and appeals; this new program offers payments at the charging stage. This marks a significant shift in federal fraud enforcement, potentially increasing enforcement actions and associated legal risks for companies in covered sectors.

• **USITC Affirms Antidumping and Countervailing Duties on Chinese Imports:** The U.S. International Trade Commission (USITC) made affirmative determinations on October 21, 2026, in five-year (sunset) reviews concerning imports from China. The USITC concluded that revoking the existing antidumping duty order on diamond sawblades and parts thereof from China, and the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on chassis and subassemblies from China, would likely lead to the continuation or recurrence of material injury to domestic industries. As a result, the existing duties on these products will remain in place. These decisions signal a continued U.S. stance on trade protection against specific Chinese goods, affecting import costs and the competitive landscape for manufacturers in these sectors.

• **Executive Order 14436 Modifies Sanctions and Duties Under Graham Act:** Executive Order 14436, "Implementing the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026," was referenced in the Federal Register on October 21, 2026, and originally signed on September 18, 2026, with a waiver issued on October 17, 2026. The order details a waiver of certain sanctions, restrictions, and duties under the Graham Act while simultaneously imposing new measures. Specifically, the order increases the rate of duty on goods from the Russian Federation by 500 percent ad valorem and on crude oil and natural gas from the largest five importers of Russian crude oil and natural gas by 100 percent ad valorem if those countries knowingly make new purchases of crude oil or natural gas that originated in the Russian Federation on or after October 18, 2026. This complex action reflects a calibrated approach to sanctions policy, intensifying economic pressure on specific Russian-related trade while providing presidential discretion on other aspects of the Act.

Why it matters: The most significant US policy shift this week involves a dual approach to international economic pressure through enhanced sanctions on Iran's illicit trade and a complex executive order adjusting tariffs and waivers under the Russia and Iran Sanctions Act, alongside a new domestic whistleblower program to combat fraud.
